findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a cutting board being stored behind the faucet handles of the triple sink. Shown to the PIC and the board was removed and placed in different location that doesn’t expose the food contact surface to contamination. Ensure that cutting boards are never stored behind faucet handles to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Two not in use mop heads were observed stored inside of mop buckets containing waste water. Shown to the PIC and the mop heads were placed on the walls of the mop sink to dry properly. Ensure that not in use mop heads are never stored in wastewater and are placed in a positions that allows for proper drying.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: A cardboard box storing chicken fat was observed with a significant amount of black mold on the outer surfaces (inside walk-in cooler). Shown to person-in-charge and the fat was transferred into a different container and the box was discarded. Ensure that food intended for public consumption is stored in a manner where it isn’t exposed to cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Various Time/Temperature Control (TCS) foods were probed between 51F - 54F inside of the walk in cooler. These items include cream cheese, raw meats, seafood, eggs, and other dairy products. It appears that the walk in unit is failing, as the ambient temperature was measured at 57F. See violation #33 for further details. Discussed that TCS foods will need to be discarded and not used for service. TCS foods were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods are held at 41F or below to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow-up on 1/15/2025.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The walk in cooler’s ambient temperature was measured at 57F (also reading at 57F for internal thermometer). Various TCS foods such as cream cheese, crab rangoon, meats, seafood, eggs, etc. were being cold held in the cooler. The person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that the facility noticed the cooler running a little high earlier in the morning. TCS foods were probed between 51F - 54F. Most TCS foods had been in the cooler overnight. A technician was contacted to service the cooler. Discussed that all TCS foods that were in the cooler overnight must be discarded. Will follow-up on 1/22/2025 to ensure that cooler is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: There isn’t any hot water available at the handwashing and the triple sink in the kitchen area. Discussed with the PIC that hot water is needed for handwashing and ware-washing purposes. A technician was contacted to service the water heater. Ensure that hot water is available at all times to be sure that hands and dishes are getting washed properly and also to reduce the spread of any pathogens that are present. Will follow-up on 1/22/2025.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(A) Capacity. (A) The water source and system shall be of sufficient capacity to meet the peak water demands of the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A bottle of mayonnaise and honey mustard was stored on the counter across from the cookline. The honey mustard bottle indicated that the sauce must be refrigerated after opening. Discussed with PIC that sauces must be either cold held or used as Time Control to ensure safety of food products. The sauces will be placed on time as control (same as other sauces that are already placed on time control) and left on the counter for no longer than 4 hours at a time. After 4 hours, the sauces will be discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Upon arrival, there was a giant stock pot of cooked chicken stored on the floor of the kitchen. PIC mentioned that the chicken was recently taken from the cooler to be reheated. Discussed never storing food on the floor and the possibility of cross contamination. The pot was moved to the stovetop to be reheated. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles and ansul of the hood system were starting to form grease droplets. PIC mentioned that the facility is expecting a technician to service the hood system soon. Discussed manually cleaning baffles in triple sink between professional cleaning services. Ensure that non-food contact services of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent grease buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed a container of eggs stored on the bottom shelf of a prep table to temp at 68F. PIC mentioned that eggs were left on shelf overnight. Eggs were discarded. Ensure that eggs are always cold held at 45F or less and never kept unrefrigerated overnight.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(B) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (B) EGGS that have not been treated to destroy all viable Salmonellae shall be stored in refrigerated EQUIPMENT that maintains an ambient air temperature of 7°C (45°F) or less.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Nonfood contact surfaces of the ice machine were observed to have an accumulation of debris on the inside surfaces. The accumulated surfaces were shown to the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of the ice machine are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
One of the kitchen employees isn't food manager or food handler certified. Ensure that employees who handle food are handler certified if not manager certified.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Observed there to be no sanitizer buckets present in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and a sani bucket was prepared and tested at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that sani buckets are present all hours of operation to properly sanitize surfaces.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the top inner surface of the microwave to be accumulated with soil in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and microwave was cleaned with a sani towel. Ensure that the inside surfaces of the microwave are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent soil buildup. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed a box of cigarettes to be placed on a dry storage rack where dry goods are being stored. The cigarettes were picked up by an employee. Ensure that personal items such as tobacco products, drinks, and food are stored separate from items intended for public consumption to protect against contamination. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed employees who are not food manager certified to not have a food handler certification. There are currently 2 CFMs at this facility. Ensure that all employees who are not CFPMs are food handler certified if they will be handling food. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed various types of milks to not be date marked in a prep cooler. Discussed with PIC and milks were marked with the appropriate date. Ensure that milks being held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a container of soy milk to be expired in a prep cooler. The manufacturer’s use-by-date was March 27, 2024. PIC discarded the soy milk. Ensure that milks do not exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed several packages of beef in the process of being thawed at room temperature. Discussed different options of approved thawing methods with PIC. Most of the beef packages were still semi frozen and were placed into the walk in cooler to complete the thawing process. Ensure that TCS foods are thawed by approved methods and not thawed at room temperature. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Observed several wiping cloths in a container that stores clean utensils. PIC noted that towels are used to dry drinking cups. The cloths were removed. Ensure that used wiping cloths are stored in a manner that prevents them from contaminating food contact surfaces. 

4-901.12: Wiping cloths laundered in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT without mechanical dryer shall be air-dried in location and manner that prevents contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. Wiping cloths may be stored in sanitizer solution after laundering.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed a box of plastic utensils in a box placed on the counter for customers to grab. Discussed with PIC to place the utensils in containers faced down or either behind the counter and out of customers’ reach. Ensure that single service utensils are stored in a manner that prevents the from contamination.  

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed mop heads to be stored inside of a mop bucket. Discussed with PIC and mop heads were positioned upright. Ensure that used mop heads are stored in a manner that allows them to properly air dry. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
(Pf) 2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, proper glove use, and cross contamination. Working supplies of TCS foods were held at room temperature during service without an established time control policy. PIC was also unfamiliar with employee health policy and did not have documentation. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the followup inspection in 10 days. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
(Pf) 2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents were not available, and PIC seemed to be unfamiliar with the requirement. Employee health was discussed. Copies of documents were provided in simplified Chinese and Spanish for current staff as well as English in case needed in the future. PIC was advised to maintain documentation at the facility and have all staff review and sign reporting agreements before followup inspection in 10 days. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
(Pf) 2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
(c) 2-401.11 1) Personal drinks were observed throughout the kitchen. An open bottle of water was observed on a shelf intermixed with single service items. Another personal drink in what appeared to be a travel cup at the kitchen entrance was spilled on the prep table while working. Proper storage of personal beverages was discussed, and drinks were moved to a lower shelf of a storage cart during inspection.
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

2) PIC began chewing a piece of gum prior to entering the kitchen and was asked to discard the gum. Inspector had to ask again later for gum to be discarded. Gum should not be chewed by staff while working. 
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
(P) 2-301.14 Handwashing did not occur prior to putting on gloves or between glove changes for staff. PIC was advised on when to wash hands and asked to educate and re-train staff on when to wash and proper handwashing technique. PIC stated she would speak with staff.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
(c) 6-301.14 Handwashing sign was not posted in restroom used by employees in the gaming area. Handwashing sign was provided to be posted.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
(P) 3-304.11 1) Unpackaged portion of seaweed was observed in a box in the prep area. PIC indicated it was for easy access but was advised the box is not considered clean or an appropriate storage location for unpackaged foods. Seaweed was discarded. Use of food grade bags (Ziplock food storage) or food service containers were discussed.

2) Unpackaged, cut raw meats were observed in plastic grocery bags in the chest freezers. PIC was advised that food grade storage bags or food containers need to be used for storage of unpackaged foods, including raw meats. Provide proper storage containers or bags by next inspection. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
(P) 3-304.15(A) Employee was observed removing jackets from a shelf in the prep area with gloved hands. Employee then returned to noodle prep area without a glove change. PIC was advised of the issue and had the employee change their gloves before continuing with next task.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
(P) 3-304.11 Fly strips with dead insects were observed throughout the kitchen above food prep and handling areas and adjacent to single service items. PIC had staff take down fly strips during inspection. Use of fly strips in appropriate locations was discussed.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(Pf) 4-601.11 Food contact surfaces and general surfaces of slicer were soiled with stuck on food debris. PIC stated slicer was last used approximately 5 or 6 days prior to slice raw beef. Cleaning and sanitizing of slicer between uses was discussed. Slicer was removed from prep area for cleaning.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize the slicer immediately after use.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
(Pf) 3-501.17 Cream bases drink mixes prepared on a previous operating day were observed without date marks in the walk-in cooler. Dating was discussed. Ensure drink mixes and all prepared foods are properly dated.
A Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
(Pf) 3-501.19 (A) & (B) Portions of fried chicken pieces and fried tofu were not being properly hot held. Products were observed out on a prep table with surface and internal temperatures ranging from 83F-97F. PIC indicated the intent was to prepare small portions and hold them at room temperature for use. PIC stated the products are typically gone within an hour or a little longer. Based on information provided, tofu was fried around 12pm and chicken was fried around 1pm. Foods were labeled with the time and were to be used or discarded within 4 hours. PIC was advised a time control policy will be established and a copy will be provided at the followup inspection in 10 days. 
Except as specified under (D) of this section, if time without temperature control is used as the public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food before cooking, or for ready to eat TCS food that is displayed or held for sale or service: (1) Written procedures shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request that specify: (a) Methods of compliance with Subparagraphs (B)(1)-(4) or (C)(1)-(5) of this section; and (b) Methods of compliance with § 3-501.14 for food that is prepared, cooked, and refrigerated before time is used as a public health control. 
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (1) The food shall have an initial temperature of 41F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 135F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control; (2) The food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; (3) The food shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if ready to eat, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; and (4) The food in unmarked containers or packages, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
(c) 4-904.11 Utensils for customer use were observed with food contact surfaces presented up in a storage container. Proper storage with handles presented up was discussed. PIC positioned utensils to allow for proper storage with handles presented out.
Sanitized utensils shall be handled so that contamination of food- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
(c) 4-501.18 Wash solution in 3 part sink was greasy and heavily soiled. Solution was emptied and basins were cleaned prior to setting up fresh solutions for ware washing.
The wash, rinse, and sanitize solutions shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
(Pf) 4-302.14 Facility had a set of chlorine test strips, but the comparison chart was not available. PIC was advised to purchase a new test kit and maintain the case with the chart so the concentration of solutions can be verified. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
(c) 6-305.11 Employee jackets were observed on top of single service items in the kitchen. An employee removed the jackets from the area. Jackets were later observed on top of packaged foods in the dry storage area. Jackets were removed from the kitchen upon request of inspector. PIC was advised staff need to store personal belongings separate from food, equipment, and single service articles. 
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.
